summary: Add Core-owned pool member join and remote repository reconciliation safeguards.

guide.reason: Local authenticated join and NFS/SMB member access are documented as development workflows with executed disposable-lab scenarios and explicit Phase 4 limits.

api.reason: The Core local and peer join/reconciliation contracts changed; the API reference update is owned by the shared API documentation lane.

roadmap.reason: Scoped BUG-0094 acceptance does not complete the remaining Phase 4 roadmap gates; the authorized advance is assessed in the bug-ledger acceptance plan record.

state.reason: Pool membership, peer trust, desired remote repositories and member access results are durable Core records.
state.record: Each Core keeps private peer identity, pending CSR/rehome and membership in <agent-state>/pool-peer.json. The master's desired NFS/SMB registrations live in <agent-state>/managed-vms; <agent-state>/pool-storage.json retains per-member access, reservations and mutation markers. Members persist reconciled repository records in <agent-state>/managed-vms and member-scoped SMB receipts in <agent-state>/storage-credentials. Authenticated Inventory.managed membership/storage reports are the fresh Controller adoption path, preserving pool, repository, credential receipt and VM IDs without Controller-held desired state.

verification.method: Focused Go suites and both Core binaries passed before the disposable two-Core lab. The primary then executed authenticated join; browser-selected NFS/SMB directory registration; member mount/identity/QEMU/lock access; one member VM per repository; in-use detach refusal; master peer outage/recovery with SMB VM survival; permission failure/recovery; two-generation offline catch-up and unused detach; fresh Controller database/TLS replacement with inventory/browser verification. No migration, HA, fencing, physical-hardware or UEFI acceptance is claimed.
